title: The Last Oath Again
premise: Mirabel Oyelaran has spent their whole life in the valley of Ashenmere, where an old covenant suppresses magic and keeps its people invisible to prophecy. When a scholar fleeing the usurper's purge arrives with a century-old book that names Mirabel by face and deed, they learn the valley's safety was always a bargain: someone born there must one day carry a message out through a country that was erased from maps and memory. Hunted by the usurper's inquisitors and guided by beasts who alone remember the lost roads, Mirabel gathers a ragged found family of exiles, deserters, and a rival beast-speaker. In the end, they reach the free cities not as a savior but as a witness—delivering the book's final page, which rewrites the prophecy itself—and pay the price of survival by surrendering the valley's protection forever, choosing justice outside any law over the comfort of being unseen.
about_author: Odile Okonkwo is a Nigerian-British writer who grew up between Lagos and Manchester, collecting folktales from both grandmothers before learning to write her own. A former archivist, she writes fantasy about people history tried to forget.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. We meet Ashenmere: a valley where magic cannot follow, where Mirabel secretly speaks with animals and hides it even from their adoptive mothers. A wounded stranger, the scholar Idris, collapses at the market carrying a locked book. Emotional beat: the ache of belonging somewhere built on forgetting.

chapters.title: A Face Written Down
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. He opens the prophetic book and finds a sketch of Mirabel dated a hundred years past, alongside a warning about 'the door out of a country that no longer exists.' The elders demand the book be burned; Idris refuses. Emotional beat: dread curdling into defiance.

chapters.title: What the Crows Remembered
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The crows tell Mirabel of soldiers crossing the northern pass—the usurper's inquisitors have learned of the book. The elders vote to expel Idris; Mirabel chooses to flee with him instead. Emotional beat: first irreversible choice, leaving found family behind.

chapters.title: The Country With No Name
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Beyond the pass lies Ossuary, a nation erased from every map, its roads known only to beasts. They are joined by Sefa, a deserter, and Wren, a child thief. Emotional beat: strangers becoming a fragile, arguing family.

chapters.title: The Other Speaker
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The party is ambushed by Kess, a rival beast-speaker serving the inquisitors, who once shared Mirabel's gift and chose power over silence. Kess spares them—for now—to deliver a message: come home, or be unmade. Emotional beat: envy and recognition between two versions of one life.

chapters.title: Doors in the Bone Hills
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Guided by an ancient badger, they find the fabled door—a gate sealed since Ossuary fell, opened only by a name no living person knows. The book hints the name died with the last king. Emotional beat: hope sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: The Price of the Gate
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The inquisitors catch them; Idris burns the decoy pages and dies buying time, revealing with his last breath that the door answers not a king's name but a witness's oath. Emotional beat: grief as inheritance—the first true cost of survival.

chapters.title: An Oath Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. At the gate, Kess returns with the inquisitor host. Instead of fighting, Mirabel swears the old oath aloud—not for a crown but for the erased dead, naming Ossuary so it exists again in speech. The gate opens; Kess wavers. Emotional beat: justice claimed beyond any law's permission.

chapters.title: The Page That Rewrites Itself
chapters.summary: Kess's POV. Inside the gate, the book's final page reveals the prophecy was never fixed—it ends blank until spoken by the one who arrives. Kess defects, holding the inquisitors at the threshold while Mirabel speaks the valley's secret into the record. Emotional beat: betrayal reversed into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Witness
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. They reach the free cities as the usurper's armies mass, delivering the rewritten prophecy that names the valley and its people to the world—ending its invisibility forever. Mirabel sends word home: the price is paid, the door stands open. Emotional beat: bittersweet arrival; survival means being seen at last.
